arxiv-2111-06599.title: PESTO: Switching Point based Dynamic and Relative Positional Encoding for Code-Mixed Languages
arxiv-2111-06599.creator: Mohsin Ali, Kandukuri Sai Teja, Sumanth Manduru, Parth Patwa, Amitava Das
arxiv-2111-06599.description: Abstract NLP applications for code-mixed (CM) or mix-lingual text have gained a significant momentum recently, the main reason being the prevalence of language mixing in social media communications in multi-lingual societies like India, Mexico, Europe, parts of USA etc. Word embeddings are basic building blocks of any NLP system today, yet, word embedding for CM languages is an unexplored territory.

arxiv-2205-12006.title: Neur2SP : Neural Two-Stage Stochastic Programming
arxiv-2205-12006.creator: Justin Dumouchelle, Rahul PatelElias B. KhalilMerve BodurDepartment of Mechanical & Industrial Engineering, University of Toronto
arxiv-2205-12006.description: Abstract Stochastic Programming is a powerful modeling framework for decision-making under uncertainty. In this work, we tackle two-stage stochastic programs (2SPs), the most widely used class of stochastic programming models. Solving 2SPs exactly requires optimizing over an expected value function that is computationally intractable.

arxiv-2304-12323.title: Squire’s theorem for nonlinear monotone energy stability
arxiv-2304-12323.creator: Giuseppe Mulone
arxiv-2304-12323.description: Abstract The Squire’s theorem holds for parallel shear flows governed by the linearized Navier-Stokes equations. Squire writes “For the study of the stability of flow between parallel walls it is sufficient to confine attention to disturbances of two-dimensional type”, Squire [ 2 , p. 627] .

arxiv-2308-04207.title: Robust retrieval of material chemical states in X-ray microspectroscopy
arxiv-2308-04207.creator: Ting Wang, Xiaotong Wu, Jizhou Li, Chao Wang
arxiv-2308-04207.description: Abstract X-ray microspectroscopic techniques are essential for studying morphological and chemical changes in materials, providing high-resolution structural and spectroscopic information. However, its practical data analysis for reliably retrieving the chemical states remains a major obstacle to accelerating the fundamental understanding of materials in many research fields.

arxiv-2311-15971.title: Supply Chain Due Diligence Risk Assessment for the EU: A Network Approach to estimate expected effectiveness of the planned EU directive
arxiv-2311-15971.creator: Jan Hurt 1,2 , Katharina Ledebur 1,2 , Birgit Meyer 1,3 , Klaus Friesenbichler 1,3 , Markus Gerschberger 1,4 , Stefan Thurner 1,2,5,6 , Peter Klimek 1,2,5
arxiv-2311-15971.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jan Hurt 1,2 , Katharina Ledebur 1,2 , Birgit Meyer 1,3 , Klaus Friesenbichler 1,3 , Markus Gerschberger 1,4 , Stefan Thurner 1,2,5,6 , Peter Klimek 1,2,5. Globalization has had undesirable effects on the labor standards embedded in the products we consume. This paper proposes an ex-ante evaluation of supply chain due diligence regulations, such as the EU Corporate Sustainable Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD).

arxiv-2407-06977.title: Experimental Method to Constrain Preferential Emission and Spectator Dynamics in Heavy-Ion Collisions Journal: Physics Letters B
arxiv-2407-06977.creator: Vipul Bairathi, Somadutta Bhatta
arxiv-2407-06977.description: Abstract We introduce a novel experimental method to quantify contribution of preferential emission to the pseudorapidity distribution of produced particles in heavy-ion collisions using correlations between spectator asymmetry and final-state multiplicity. Within a transport model, the magnitude of this correlator increases from mid to forward rapidities, reflecting the impact of preferential emission and capturing fluctuations in sources of particle production.

arxiv-2409-12134.title: BERT-VBD: Vietnamese Multi-Document Summarization Framework
arxiv-2409-12134.creator: Tuan-Cuong Vuong, Trang Mai Xuan, Thien Van Luong
arxiv-2409-12134.description: Abstract In tackling the challenge of Multi-Document Summarization (MDS), numerous methods have been proposed, spanning both extractive and abstractive summarization techniques. However, each approach has its own limitations, making it less effective to rely solely on either one. An emerging and promising strategy involves a synergistic fusion of extractive and abstractive summarization methods.

arxiv-2506-05864.title: CryoFastAR: Fast Cryo-EM Ab initio Reconstruction Made Easy
arxiv-2506-05864.creator: Jiakai Zhang Shouchen Zhou Haizhao Dai Xinhang Liu, Peihao Wang Zhiwen Fan Yuan Pei Jingyi Yu
arxiv-2506-05864.description: Abstract Pose estimation from unordered images is fundamental for 3D reconstruction, robotics, and scientific imaging. Recent geometric foundation models, such as DUSt3R, enable end-to-end dense 3D reconstruction but remain underexplored in scientific imaging fields like cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) for near-atomic protein reconstruction.

pmc-10800921.creator: Cheng Liang, Haoyang Xu, Hui You, Ouling Zhang, Yiman Han, Qingyu Li, Yungao Hu, Xunchao Xiang
pmc-10800921.description: Resistant starch (RS) can help prevent diabetes and decrease calorie intake and that from plants are the main source of mankind consumption. Rice is many people’s staple food and that with higher RS will help health management. A significantly positive correlation exists between apparent amylose content (AAC) of rice and its RS content.

pmc-11324758.title: Direct retino-iridal projections and intrinsic iris contraction mediate the pupillary light reflex in early vertebrates
pmc-11324758.creator: Cecilia Jiménez-López, Paula Rivas-Ramírez, Marta Barandela, Carmen Núñez-González, Manuel Megías, Juan Pérez-Fernández
pmc-11324758.description: The pupillary light reflex (PLR) adapts the amount of light reaching the retina, protecting it and improving image formation. Two PLR mechanisms have been described in vertebrates. First, the pretectum receives retinal inputs and projects to the Edinger-Westphal nucleus (EWN), which targets the ciliary ganglion through the oculomotor nerve (nIII).

pmc-11528020.title: Data collation for climate-cooling gas dimethylsulfide in Antarctic snow, sea ice and underlying seawater
pmc-11528020.creator: Gabrielle Burke, Pat Wongpan, Delphine Lannuzel, Hakase Hayashida
pmc-11528020.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Dimethylsulfide (DMS) is a climatically active volatile sulfur compound found in Earth’s oceans and atmosphere that plays an important role in cloud formation. DMS originates from its precursor dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP), which is produced by several classes of phytoplankton. Concentrations of DMS and DMSP in Antarctic sea ice, snow and underlying seawater are not well documented and there is currently no dataset available to find the existing data. The purpose of this project was to compile historical measurements into a publicly available dataset.

pmc-12522223.title: Influencing factors for childbirth readiness among pregnant women based on the reciprocal determinism theory and backpropagation neural network: a cross-sectional study in China
pmc-12522223.creator: Yuan Mengmei, Zhao Meizhen, Zeng Tieying, Wu Meiliyang, Zhang Ke
pmc-12522223.description: BackgroundChildbirth readiness is essential for improving maternal health outcomes and reducing mortality, yet preparedness remains low among pregnant women globally. This study aims to identify key factors influencing childbirth readiness among Chinese women, using reciprocal determinism theory and a backpropagation neural network.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted with 816 pregnant women from three hospitals in Hubei, China.

pmc-12537966.title: Dysfunctional digestive tract highlights the metabolic hallmarks of nanoplastic-exacerbated Parkinson’s pathology
pmc-12537966.creator: Xiufang Liang, Yue Wang, Nicholas Andrikopoulos, Pu Chun Ke, Yuhuan Li
pmc-12537966.description: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is increasingly viewed as both a neurological and metabolic disorder, with the gut-brain axis playing a key role. This study explored how polystyrene (PS) nanoplastics contributed to PD progression by examining their metabolic impact in an A53T α-synuclein (αS) mouse model.

pmc-12659732.title: Coronary angiography with photon-counting detector CT—new options and some critical decisions
pmc-12659732.creator: Victor Mergen, Matthias Eberhard, Hatem Alkadhi
pmc-12659732.description: The advent of photon-counting detector CT brought up various new interesting possibilities for coronary imaging including different scan modes and various post-processing options. The two main scan modes include spectral data acquisition with inherent energy-resolved imaging and ultra-high-resolution scanning with unprecedented high spatial resolution, both at the highest available temporal resolution.

pmc-13070293.title: Antibacterial consumption in public health facilities in Uganda: a trend analysis of national warehouse distribution data 2022–2024
pmc-13070293.creator: Benard Nsubuga, Ventrine Marion Chelimo, Aaron Kayemba, Philip Ampaire, Winnie Nambatya, Kalidi Rajab, Vivian Twemanye, Harriet Akello, Anthony Ddamba, Moses Kamabare, David Arinaitwe, Francis Kakooza, Richard Walwema
pmc-13070293.description: BackgroundWhile multiple factors contribute to antimicrobial resistance (AMR), the consumption of antimicrobials is a major modifiable cause. Therefore, accurate understanding of antibacterial exposure is critical for effective stewardship.ObjectiveThis study analysed trends of antibacterial distribution data in Uganda between 2022 and 2024.

pmc-13419090.title: An Efficient Cross-Modal Interaction and Dynamic Fusion Network for Multimodal Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis
pmc-13419090.creator: Xiangqiong Wu, Yin Lan, Lina Han, Peng Wang
pmc-13419090.description: Simple SummaryMultimodal breast ultrasound provides complementary information for lesion characterization, while effective integration remains challenging due to heterogeneous feature distributions, limited cross-modal interaction, and sensitivity to noise and missing data. This study presents an efficient framework that enhances modality-specific features, enables early-stage cross-modal interaction, and adaptively fuses multimodal information.

pmc-13522886.creator: Yimeng Zhou, Xue Meng
pmc-13522886.description: ze HCC risk stratification where vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) is unavailable. However, an important question remains regarding the applicability of these findings to patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), now the most prevalent cause of chronic liver disease worldwide. The authors' conclusion relies on two complementary yet structurally mismatched datasets.

pmc-13599992.title: Efficacy and safety of patent haemostasis-guided strategies for preventing radial artery occlusion following transradial coronary procedures: a protocol for a systematic review, network meta-analysis, and exploratory component network meta-analysis
pmc-13599992.creator: Xiaoping Guo, Fu Dai, Shuo Liang, Lingxia Fan, Wei Li
pmc-13599992.description: IntroductionPatent hemostasis (PH) is important for preventing radial artery occlusion after transradial coronary procedures, but the relative efficacy and safety of different PH-guided strategies remain uncertain. This study aims to compare and rank these strategies and, if data permit, explore the potential contributions of their key components.

pmc-13631483.title: 지워진 대안, 고착된 경로: 권위주의 정권기 의료 인력 공급 정책의 경합, 1961–1988†
pmc-13631483.creator: 승만 박
pmc-13631483.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This article traces how physician supply policy was formulated and implemented during Korea’s authoritarian era (1961–1988), spanning the military regime of Park Chung-hee and the New Military regime of Chun Doo-hwan. It examines several questions that have hitherto gone unexplained: the circumstances behind the initiation (1965), suspension (1971), and resumption (1978) of the founding of new medical schools; why most of these newly established schools were private; and the range of alternatives explored in lieu of building medical schools.

pmc-13657713.title: Transmural migration of an internal pancreaticojejunostomy stent causing delayed intra-abdominal sepsis: a case report
pmc-13657713.creator: Kamal Abi Mosleh, Ismail M Saleem, Caitlin Burns, Carolina Orsi, Hishaam Ismael
pmc-13657713.description: BackgroundInternal pancreatic duct stents are commonly used during pancreaticojejunostomy (PJ) reconstruction following pancreaticoduodenectomy to facilitate drainage and potentially reduce postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF). These stents are typically expected to migrate distally and pass without consequence. However, rare complications related to stent migration may occur and can present with atypical clinical and biochemical findings, creating diagnostic challenges.
